nodes.label: A focus ring drawn inside the button is invisible on the active button
nodes.norm_label: a focus ring drawn inside the button is invisible on the active button
nodes.rationale: The brief told the agent to draw the `.seg` ring inside the box because `overflow: hidden` clips an outside ring. It implemented that, screenshotted it in headless Firefox on a separate profile, and found the ring was not visible at all on the active button. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t6-focus-and-responsive [ses_f05ed56d3ffeekSmQQCHP8U9LS].md:L7463] Stated reason for the reversal: `--focus-ring` vs `--accent` = 1.00:1 in light mode and 1.59:1 in dark, and the active button's own background is `--accent`, so an inside ring is the same colour as the surface it sits on. The fix was the other option the brief had offered: `.seg` becomes `overflow: visible`, inner `border-radius: 9px` on `:first-child`/`:last-child`, ring drawn outside at `outline-offset: 2px`.

nodes.label: A flat brace scanner desyncs on @keyframes nesting and silently stops reading the file
nodes.norm_label: a flat brace scanner desyncs on keyframes nesting and silently stops reading the file
nodes.summary: The CSS test helper parsed style.css by finding the next `{` and then the next `}`. `@keyframes denyut { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.45; } }` has a nested block, so the scanner consumed only part of the keyframes body, pushed a rule with the selector `50%`, and then hit the leftover closing brace and returned. Both max-width media queries at the end of the file were never read, so every assertion scoped to a media query was passing against an empty set.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t6-focus-and-responsive [ses_f05ed56d3ffeekSmQQCHP8U9LS].md:L7445] Stated reason the fix had to include a new test rather than only a parser repair: two of the thirteen RED failures were caused by the test's own parser being wrong, not by the CSS, and a scanner that stops early is the failure mode that cannot be noticed because every other assertion goes green on what it did manage to read. The repair was to count brace depth instead of taking the first `}`, plus a `pemindai berkas` test that rejects `@keyframes` content leaking out as a selector so the class of failure cannot come back quietly.

nodes.label: A pseudo-class-stripping selector lookup silently returns the focus rule
nodes.norm_label: a pseudo-class stripping selector lookup silently returns the focus rule
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t6-focus-and-responsive [ses_f05ed56d3ffeekSmQQCHP8U9LS].md:L7457] Stated reason: the lookup helper `wajibDitemukan` matched selectors after throwing pseudo-classes away, and because `:focus-visible` appears later in the file than the base rules, `wajibDitemukan("#list a")` returned the `#list a:focus-visible` block. Every height computation was then made from the wrong rule block and passed with no evidence behind it. The basic lookup was changed to demand an exact match, and two new tests were added so the class of mismatch cannot recur unnoticed.

nodes.label: The planned clipped-second-line defect could not be reproduced; line-height was the real mechanism
nodes.norm_label: the planned clipped second line defect could not be reproduced line height was the real mechanism
nodes.summary: The brief and Finding 8 claimed the second line of a wrapped `#list a` report title overflowed the box and was never visible. The agent measured it and could not reproduce that: `barisDiLuarKotak = 0` in every measurement, including a three-line title under the old CSS. The real effect of the offending CSS was different.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t6-focus-and-responsive [ses_f05ed56d3ffeekSmQQCHP8U9LS].md:L7480] Stated correction: a block box with `min-height` grows rather than clipping, and the actual mechanism was that `line-height: 44px` made every line box 44px tall, so a three-line title became a 134px box (94px after the fix) with odd inter-line spacing. The fix stayed the one AC3 asked for; only the stated mechanism in the plan was wrong.

nodes.label: Mutation testing to prove tests are non-vacuous
nodes.norm_label: mutation testing to prove tests are non-vacuous
nodes.rationale: This note's own evidence for the claim, kept separate from the shadow-tree mutant run recorded in the other chunk: five temporary reverts were applied to the working tree, each one turned the specific assertions red, and all five were then restored. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t6-focus-and-responsive [ses_f05ed56d3ffeekSmQQCHP8U9LS].md:L7451] The first row of that revert table is restoring `#ask { display: none; }` to the 768px media query, which turned `#ask tidak pernah disembunyikan` red. The other four reverts put `.seg` back to `overflow: hidden` with `outline-offset: -4px`, put `#list a` back to `line-height: 44px` with `padding: 0 12px`, deleted every `:focus-visible` rule, and zeroed `.ric-gap` while setting the 480px column count to 4.

nodes.label: Package-name substring matching invents reverse-dependency edges
nodes.norm_label: package name substring matching invents reverse dependency edges
nodes.summary: A scan of `pacman -Qi` output for reverse dependencies of `bluez` used the pattern `\bbluez\b`. Because `-` is a non-word character, `bluez` inside `bluez-libs` and `bluez-qt` matched too, so `pipewire-audio` and `bluedevil` were reported as depending on `bluez`. Re-running with exact token equality produced the real chain.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-23 - review-konfigurasi-arch-linux [ses_f32050468ffeExZNTzaAlhTjZU].md:L2321] The reason this changed the plan rather than just the report: the true chain is plasma-meta to bluedevil to bluez-qt to bluez, so `pacman -Rns bluez` would have cascaded all the way to `plasma-meta`, which the user had asked to have removed. The decision became to keep the package installed and mask the service instead, since the service was already disabled.

nodes.label: systemctl is-enabled exits 0 for masked but 1 for disabled
nodes.norm_label: systemctl is enabled exit code is zero for masked but one for disabled
nodes.summary: The setup script branches on `systemctl is-enabled --quiet bluetooth.service` to decide whether Bluetooth needs disabling. Measured on this machine, `disabled` exits 1 and `masked` exits 0, so the guard treats the stricter state as the enabled one.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-23 - review-konfigurasi-arch-linux [ses_f32050468ffeExZNTzaAlhTjZU].md:L3190] The session did not take this from documentation; it created a dummy user unit, masked it, and read the exit code, getting `masked quiet exit=0` to confirm the earlier `disabled` measurement of exit 1. That is why the script masks Bluetooth rather than merely disabling it, since only the masked state reads as off to the guard.

nodes.label: Never store the backup on the partition being backed up
nodes.norm_label: never store the backup on the partition being backed up
nodes.summary: Timeshift snapshots were placed on `/home` (nvme0n1p3, 85 GB with 80 GB free) rather than on `/` (32 GB with 22 GB free), even though `/` is the filesystem actually being captured. A second, independent reason was given: filling `/` risks an unbootable system, and the safe floor was stated as roughly 5 GB free.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-23 - review-konfigurasi-arch-linux [ses_f32050468ffeExZNTzaAlhTjZU].md:L9802] Stated reason: if `/` is corrupted the snapshot dies with it, whereas on a separate `/home` you can reinstall `/` and still restore. The note also recorded the limit of the arrangement honestly, that both partitions are on the same physical NVMe, so a dead drive takes both, and timeshift is a system safety net rather than an archive for personal files.

nodes.label: Hand the user one idempotent script instead of granting temporary NOPASSWD sudo
nodes.norm_label: hand the user one idempotent script instead of granting temporary nopasswd sudo
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-23 - review-konfigurasi-arch-linux [ses_f32050468ffeExZNTzaAlhTjZU].md:L1748] The agent's terminal cannot type an interactive sudo password, and it offered two ways forward: one script the user runs once themselves, or a temporary NOPASSWD sudoers line that is removed afterwards. The user chose the script, on the stated ground that it is safest because the password never has to be shared. Two execution constraints then fell out of that choice: the script refuses to run when EUID is 0 because makepkg refuses to run as root and the AUR helper has to build as the user, and each step is guarded so a re-run reports what is already done and skips it.
